core_message: Tristan da Cunha is the most remote inhabited island group, and after a 1961 eruption forced everyone out, most islanders chose to return.
title: The Most Remote Village on Earth
description:
Tristan da Cunha, a British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic, is the most remote inhabited island group in the world. Its only settlement, Edinburgh of the Seven Seas, sits on a coastal plain beneath Queen Mary's Peak, a 2,062 m volcano, and is home to fewer than 250 people. There is no airport; Cape Town, about 2,800 km away, is roughly a week by ship. Land is held in common, families farm potatoes and keep cattle, and the population shares only a handful of surnames. In October 1961 a volcanic vent opened right beside the settlement, and the whole population was evacuated and taken to England. In 1963 most of them chose to return home.

Source: Wikipedia, Tristan da Cunha; Wikipedia, Edinburgh of the Seven Seas.

scenes.narration: This is the most remote inhabited island on Earth. Fewer than two hundred and fifty people live here, in one village at the foot of a volcano.
Tristan da Cunha has no airport. The nearest city, Cape Town, is about two thousand eight hundred kilometres away, roughly a week by ship.
The land is owned by the whole community. Families grow potatoes and keep cattle, and most islanders share just a handful of surnames.
In 1961, the volcano erupted right next to the village. Everyone was evacuated, and the whole population was taken to England.
Two years later, most of them chose to come home. And they still live there today.
